steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Cream margarine and sugar together in a medium bowl until smooth. Stir in eggs and vanilla.
Sift flour, baking soda, cloves, and cinnamon together into a bowl. Stir dry ingredients into the wet ingredients. Add bananas, oats, and chocolate chips; mix until well blended.
Drop dough by rounded spoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are golden, 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove from the oven and transfer cookies to a wire rack to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Banana Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Try this banana oatmeal cookie recipe for the best cookies (besides chocolate chip) that you will ever eat!

review.reviewBody: This makes an excellent cookie. My mother used to make a cookie like this when I was a little girl. I can't remember if her's was as cake like but I think it was close. Either way, we really love these. I did a few things different. I replaced over half of the butter with applesauce and I used brown sugar as well as white and added in some walnuts for crunch. I think the applesauce, oatmeal, and bananas makes it a good cookie to give children. It's a little healthier than your normal chocolate chip cookie! Thanks Jenny!

The recipe is good. The cookies are a little cakey but that's ok with me and my family. 
I exchanged margarine for coconut oil (but 1 cup is A LOT! I would like it to contain less fat) and I replaced 1/3 of the all-purpose flour for whole-wheat flour. Since I prepared half a batch to give it a try I used only one banana and it was perfect. The proportion of sugar for me is perfect, but some people could use a couple extra spoonfuls of sugar .
I prepared the cookies and some bars (I uploaded pictures several times accidentaly, you can see them in "more photos").

Great recipe and easy to make. Prep time a bit longer than indicated in recipe but the extra 10 minutes are not enough to skip over it. I substituted the margarine with unsalted butter, the chocolate chips with chopped raisins (because that is what I had on hand) and added a generous pinch of ground black pepper. Also, I use parchment paper for all my backing and it works great with this recipe too. One cookie sheet of this first batch was gone before the last one was done baking :)

Wonderful! I made some substitutions, some of which were my own doing, some recommended. I used softened salted butter because it's all I had. I also realized my husband used the last of the eggs for breakfast so I used a single serving container of Motts applesauce (I'm sure sweetened) as an egg substitute. Not knowing how much the salted butter or the sweetness of the applesauce would affect the taste, I used 1/2 c white sugar and 1/4 c brown sugar. Also, I substituted the clove for 1/2 t. of nutmeg. Last, but not least, I only had 2 ripe bananas left to use for this recipe. Typically, cake like cookies are not my favorite, however, I made these to be breakfast cookies and they were PERFECT. For half of the batch (for myself and the hubs) I added walnuts and a handful of Craisins. Yummy! I will be making again!

Subbed butter for margarine, did 1/2 cup each white and brown sugar, used chopped pecans instead of chocolate chips, used only 1/2 tsp cloves and added a bit of allspice and ginger. Very tasty, but more like muffin tops than “cookies”. I might try some other healthy subs (replacing some of the fat with applesauce, reducing sugar) to make it more of a healthy breakfast option.
This is a delicious soft cookie. The spices are present but not overpowering. I modified it by using an all purpose Gluten-Free flour (King Arthur's) plus 1/2 tsp xanthan gum (for stability).

Very simple & delicious. I'm don't like chocolate chips with bananas so added 2 cups walnut pieces instead. Added 1 extra ripe banana & used nutmeg instead of cloves. It's very much the texture of a soft & moist muffin top. Even though I made some changes, it's only for personal taste. Still a 5 star cookie recipe. Baked for 12 mins & as always, I don't use my convection setting when baking.

I debated rating this recipe since I revised it so much but I did enjoy my cookies so I decided to share anyway. I know most banana and oat cookies are cake like which I still enjoy. However, it has been my experience the more bananas included the less likely for it to taste as well after a couple of days, so I only put in one banana. To add some additional flavor I put a couple tsps of coffee to the mashed banana (I got this idea from a muffin recipe that had turned out well) and let it sit for 10 minutes before commencing with the rest of the recipe. For the spices I did 1/4 tsp cloves, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1/2 tsp nutmeg. I didn't think chocolate chips sounded very good with those spices so I did as another suggested and added dried cranberries and dried blueberries (technically mine were cranberries that were "blueberry juice infused" by ocean spray). To cut some additional calories I cut down on the margarine to 3/4 cup and the sugar to 3/4 cup as well as changing to 1/2 cup brown sugar 1/4 cup regular sugar. On top of all these changes I also tested out the quantity of the oats. I did the batch with 1 cup then split the batch in half and added 1/2 cup oats to one batch and left the other half as is with 1 cup's worth of oats. I thought both batches turned out well to me the additional oats made the cookies slightly more cake like but my hubby said the opposite. As I enjoyed the one with less oats more but my husband with more oats I will make again the same way.

Very delicious!
My mom and sisters loved the recipe.
I made half in a cookie sheet and half in a cupcake sheet so those came out like cute muffins.
I added some shredded coconut on top before placing into the oven and a piece of walnut, made it look elegantly pretty!
Also a little powered sugar when out the oven.
Thanks for the recipe!!

I love this recipe; it makes great, fluffy muffin-like cookies.

I replace the choc chips for dried fruits such as dates and raisins. I also replace the cloves for nutmeg and keep the cinnamon as well. 

So yummy!

I thought this was a good recipe. I changed a couple things...instead of 1C sugar I used 3/4C white sugar 1/4C brown sugar. I used real butter instead of margerine. I also separated the batch in two and did half with chocolate chips & half with walnuts & cranberries. I preferred the walnut/cranberry ones better.
OK, I changed a few things. I used butter instead of margarine, added a cup of raisins and two cups of walnuts and left out the chocolate chips.
super tasty but definitely more of a cake or bread texture, rather then a cookie
Hate to say it but they were tasteless. Needed a scoop of peanut butter or chocolate chips.
I used half white and half brown sugar. I didnt use chocolate chips but added chopped nuts. Cookies aren't overly sweet and nice with a cup of coffee. Nothing real special but they are good.
I added chopped walnuts for that "extra" banana bread flavor!!!
Excellent recipe. Prepared and baked as written. except used half white sugar and half brown sugar.
They turned out good but I personally do not like the taste. My family did like them but most will be going to work for them to try.
